newsitem.title: UK: FedEx announce new initiatives for Europe.
newsitem.headline: FedEx announce new initiatives for Europe.

text.p: Federal Express Corp said on Tuesday it would introduce major new initiatives for companies shipping into Europe.
U.S. integrator, FedEx, will upgrade its intercontinental delivery service in key commercial centres, from 12.00 noon to 10.30am, effective November 1, the statement said.

The cities covered by the new 10.30am delivery service include Brussels, Antwerp, Paris, Amsterdam, Eindhoven, Milan, Geneva, Zurich, Basel, Cologne, Dusseldorf, Hamburg, Frankfurt, Munich, Stuttgart and London.

Following the successful launch of FedEx International First, its 8.00am next day delivery service to the U.S., an 8.00am inbound service to a number of cities in Europe is also planned for early 1997, it added.
FedEx feel the new service will be of special interest to European companies that import on a "just-in-time" basis from around the world.
Receiving such shipments much earlier in the morning will give them greater flexibility, especially when they need to work on an inbound shipment and export it that same day, the statement said.

FedEx vice president, marketing and customer service, Paul Evans said: "Speed to market is increasingly important for many companies, especially those who ship time sensitive products." - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
